subject: Hosted API vendor pricing comparison & matching request
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@unifyhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API vendor pricing comparison & matching request

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing our vendor shortlist for the hosted API that will power UnifyHealth's virtual triage assistant. Procurement asked me to gather a quick apples-to-apples comparison across pricing and packaging. A few notes from the vendors we've already gotten preliminary terms from: OpenAI (committed tier offer), Anthropic (enterprise bundle), and AWS Bedrock partners.

What we need from Redwood (short):
- Full hosted API rate card (token and embedding units) and any volume/term discounts you can offer for a 12-month commit (we estimate ~1.2M text requests/month, mixed chat & completion; embeddings ~10M vectors/month).
- Any SKU-level differences (e.g., streaming vs non-streaming pricing, early-exit token billing, embedding unit definitions).
- Whether you can match or structure parity with specific line items from other vendors — procurement will push for best-in-class unit economics.
- Any limits or SLO commitments we should be aware of (burst behavior, regional routing, maintenance windows).

Attached is a short template procurement asked us to populate — it's intentionally simple. If you can return a completed version and a short narrative on where Redwood wins (performance, caching/latency, failover) vs competitors that would help our internal scoring.

We are aiming to complete vendor conversations by 2027-09-20. Would you have a 30-minute slot next week to review pricing and any customization options?

Appreciate it —
Laura Chen
Head of Procurement, UnifyHealth
laura.chen@unifyhealth.com

Attachments: UnifyHost-requested-quote.pdf (template), internal procurement checklist
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API vendor pricing comparison & matching request

Karthik / Vivek — forwarding UnifyHealth's note. They want a completed line-item comparison and to know whether we can match the economics they're getting from OpenAI/Anthropic/AWS partners.

Quick context: UnifyHealth is evaluating a triage assistant (high embedding volume, moderate-text generation). They care about predictable hosted pricing, regional routing in US, and SOC2 evidence. Procurement timeline is tight — decision window closes 9/20.

Ask: can you two review and propose 2 commercial options we can send back by end of day tomorrow:
1) Aggressive match option (what discount/commit term required to be price-competitive on token + embeddings)
2) Differentiated value option (moderate discount + product guarantees: fallback routing, prefix caching, model selection policies)

Also: Vivek, please advise on whether Dedicated/Private SKUs would materially change the numbers here if they prefer reserved capacity vs hosted. Karthik, please prepare the filled comparison template (I've attached) and a short one-pager on where Redwood outperforms (latency / cache / routing).

I'll own the customer call scheduling once we have the options.

Thanks —
Irene
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-09-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API vendor pricing comparison & matching request

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear template and timeline. Apologies for the short turnaround; please find an initial return below and two options attached (PDF + comparison spreadsheet).

Quick summary (high level):
- Baseline hosted API (public catalog model family): $0.019 / 1k prompt tokens and $0.024 / 1k completion tokens. Embeddings: $0.0009 / vector for the mixed-usage embedding SKU. These are our public list numbers; detailed line items are in the attached ratecard.
- Option A (Match-First): 12-month commitment, 1.0M avg requests/month (min 1.2M in month 3+), 18% committed discount on both token and embedding SKUs. This gets us within procurement range of the committed offers you mentioned. Requires a signed MSA addendum and 30 days notice for early termination.
- Option B (Value-Plus): 12-month commitment, 10% committed discount + product guarantees: 99.9% regional availability SLO, automatic model fallback to smaller quantized variants during capacity events, and priority routing to avoid noisy-neighbor latency spikes. Also includes a quarterly health report and a 2-week free trial of our Dedicated burst pool (no extra charge for 2 weeks).

Notes on comparisons:
- Billing semantics: we bill per-token including final tokens; streaming vs non-streaming is the same token accounting. Embedding units are per-vector. The attached spreadsheet maps each competitor line item to Redwood's SKU for a direct match.
- TCO: because of our prefix and KV caching on long-lived sessions, customers with stateful chat patterns typically see 10-30% fewer billed tokens vs raw competitor sampling for the same user experience. We called that out in the TCO tab.
- Security & compliance: we will provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and can support KMS integrations for keys on Private/Dedicated.

Attachments included: Redwood-hosted-ratecard-Q3-2027.pdf, unify-pricing-comparison-template.xlsx

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute pricing review with you and procurement on 2027-09-16 between 09:00-11:00 PT? I'll bring Karthik and Vivek. If that window doesn't work, propose alternatives and we'll adapt.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Enterprise Sales
irene.choi@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
